stem: A tool crosses a quarantine boundary without the required sanitation step. What is the correct record response?
choices: Sanitize the tool later and omit the crossing if no contamination becomes visible.
Remove the tool from inventory so the record no longer shows a quarantine-boundary violation.
Treat the event as a biosecurity deviation, apply the supplied containment/correction procedure, and document what crossed the boundary and what actions followed.
Assume the event had no consequence because no pest was visible on the tool.
rationale: Crossing a quarantine boundary without the required sanitation step is a process failure even if no organism is visible. The event should remain reconstructable so the facility can determine affected scope and corrective action. Silent cleanup or deleting the tool record hides the deviation.
